name: liftli
description: AI ghostwriter that grows you on LinkedIn and X, and writes your Substack: strategy, ideas, posts, publishing and analytics.

interface.longDescription:
Liftli is your AI ghostwriter for LinkedIn, X and Substack. It plans your content, finds ideas in your real work, writes in your voice, publishes after you approve, and learns what works.

Built for founders, consultants and professionals who want to grow on LinkedIn and X without spending hours on content or paying a human ghostwriter.

How it works:
1. Strategy: Liftli learns your positioning, audience and writing voice, and builds your content strategy: content pillars, posting cadence and a content calendar.
2. Ideas from your day-to-day: it turns what actually happened in your week (a customer call, a meeting, a release, a voice note, this week's news in your field) into post ideas, and keeps them between conversations.
3. Writing in your voice: LinkedIn posts, comments and articles, X posts and threads, Substack newsletters and Notes. Every draft is critiqued against a hook and structure rubric and fact-checked before it goes out, so it sounds like you, not like AI.
4. Publishing: post now or schedule to LinkedIn and X through their official APIs, only after you approve each post.
5. Analytics: log results and read your LinkedIn analytics to learn what works for your audience, and use it in your next posts.

Also:
- Design LinkedIn carousels and article cover images with your exact words
- Repurpose one idea across LinkedIn, X and Substack
- Rewrite your LinkedIn profile: headline, About and Featured
- Write posts and articles that AI search engines can cite (GEO and AEO)

Nothing publishes without your explicit approval.

positive.description: Turn a saved idea into a LinkedIn post, review it and save it as a draft.
positive.prompt: Turn my saved idea about the monthly close into a LinkedIn post, critique it, and save it as a draft.
positive.tools_triggered: recall, plan_post, critique, ready_to_post (ChatGPT sometimes calls strategist_briefing first)
positive.expected_behavior: Finds Sam's saved idea "the monthly close is too slow to run a DTC business on", returns a post plan; ChatGPT drafts the post, Liftli scores it, and the draft that passes is saved. Nothing is published.

positive.description: Build a LinkedIn content strategy and save it.
positive.prompt: Build me a LinkedIn content strategy with 3 or 4 pillars and a weekly posting cadence, and save it to Liftli.
positive.tools_triggered: playbook, save_strategy (ChatGPT sometimes calls strategist_briefing first)
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the strategy brief from Sam's profile; ChatGPT proposes 3 or 4 pillars and a weekly cadence for CFOs at DTC brands and saves them to Liftli.

positive.description: Critique a saved draft and suggest a stronger hook.
positive.prompt: Critique my draft about our forecast error and suggest a stronger hook.
positive.tools_triggered: recall, critique (ChatGPT sometimes calls strategist_briefing first)
positive.expected_behavior: Finds Sam's saved draft "We publish our forecast error: under 5% at 30 days", returns weighted scores, a verdict and specific fixes; ChatGPT proposes a stronger hook. Nothing is published.

positive.description: Plan a LinkedIn post from a lesson in real client work.
positive.prompt: I want to share a lesson from this week's client call on LinkedIn. What should I post?
positive.expected_behavior: Uses Sam's saved idea from the CFO call that caught a November cash gap; returns a post plan and ChatGPT drafts the post in Sam's voice. Nothing is published.

positive.prompt: Help me write this week's newsletter for my Substack readers: why the monthly close is too slow for DTC brands
positive.tools_triggered: plan_post, critique, ready_to_post, save_post (ChatGPT sometimes calls strategist_briefing first)
positive.expected_behavior: Asks which angle this issue takes (grounded in Sam's saved idea). After the user picks one, ChatGPT drafts the issue, critique reviews it until it passes, ready_to_post saves the reviewed body and save_post adds the title and subtitle. Nothing is published.
